title: Dashboard: Object Gateway Service is not configured after upgrade to helm v1.11.4
body: I upgraded my Helm-installed Rook cluster from v1.11.3 to v1.11.4. All pods are running, and the dashboard lists two object gateways, but the Object Gateway section says that the Object Gateway Service is not configured and reports an error connecting to it. The gateway itself appears to work because I can see successful requests in its logs. I can share logs, but I do not know which module's logs are needed.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading Rook from v1.11.3 to v1.11.4, all pods are running and the dashboard lists two object gateways, but opening the Object Gateway section shows 'The Object Gateway Service is not configured' and an error connecting to the gateway.
The gateway continues to handle requests successfully according to its logs.
N0.label: N0 dashboard cannot connect to working object gateway

symptoms_visible: When I try to roll back to the previous version, the monitor processes abort while decoding the authentication key state.
N1_x.label: N1_x rollback aftermath with monitor crashes

symptoms_visible: With the cluster back on the newer stack, the Object Gateway page still reports a connection error while gateway requests continue to succeed.
The manager log says it found RGW on common-kuber-01 and common-kuber-03 at port 8080, then gets 'Connection refused' while requesting the RGW admin endpoint.
N2.label: N2 manager RGW connection failure captured

symptoms_visible: The dashboard manager is trying to contact Kubernetes node names on port 8080 rather than the working in-cluster gateway endpoint, and the connection is refused.
N3.label: N3 affected Ceph version and incorrect endpoint established

symptoms_visible: A maintainer reports that a Rook release now comes with the Ceph dashboard fix for this RGW endpoint problem, but I have not reported retesting that release on my cluster.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix available but original reporter has not verified

solution.intent: Roll back the Rook and Ceph deployment to the previously used versions to restore the old dashboard behavior.
solution.concrete_example: Roll the Helm deployment back to Rook v1.11.3 and its earlier Ceph image.

edges.comment: Reporter c0 tried the rollback on the opening reporter's cluster. Reporter c8 confirmed that the resulting monitor abort matched the CryptoKey/KeyServer decode failure quoted in c7, so downgrade is a falsified remedy for this cluster.

question_patterns: After returning the cluster to an operational version, can you share the Ceph manager logs from when you open the Object Gateway page?
What does the active mgr pod log when the dashboard attempts to connect to RGW?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have the same manager log. It finds RGW with host=common-kuber-01 and host=common-kuber-03, port=8080, ssl=False. It then requests http://common-kuber-03:8080/admin/metadata/user?myself and gets '[Errno 111] Connection refused'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The manager log connects successfully to the RGW admin endpoint and returns HTTP 200; the dashboard then fails with a frontend JavaScript error.
The same node-host endpoint is logged, but the failure is 'Name or service not known' instead of 'Connection refused'.

solution.intent: Recover from the incompatible downgrade by returning to the newer operational Ceph stack, then diagnose the dashboard failure from the active manager log.
solution.concrete_example: Do not leave the monitors on the crashing older image. Return to the newer operational image, reproduce the dashboard error, and collect the active mgr pod log.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter only confirmed the monitor's CryptoKey/KeyServer decode crash. Interpreting this as an authentication-state format incompatibility caused by downgrading is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Reporter c5 supplied this manager log from the original reporter's cluster after c1 requested logs. Returning to an operational stack is implied by the later running mgr log after the failed rollback; the endpoint and connection error are kept as raw reporter evidence.

question_patterns: What are common-kuber-01 and common-kuber-03 in your deployment?
Are the hostnames in the manager log RGW service names, pod names, or Kubernetes node names?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: common-kuber-01 and common-kuber-03 are my Kubernetes node names.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Those names are the resolvable Kubernetes Services for the two gateways, and port 8080 is their configured service port.

question_patterns: Which Ceph image version is the affected cluster running?
Can you check the Ceph version associated with the working cluster state?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The affected deployment is using Ceph v17.2.6, which became the default with the upgrade.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The cluster is still using Ceph v17.2.5; only the Rook operator image changed.
The image is another build of Ceph v17.2.6 with the same manager log behavior.

edges.comment: Reporter c5 explicitly identified common-kuber-01 and common-kuber-03 as node names and discussed Ceph v17.2.6 as the new default. Similar reports from participants c2, c6, c20, and c38 corroborate the same node-host/port behavior on their own deployments but are not spliced into the reporter's setup.

solution.intent: Treat this as a Ceph dashboard RGW endpoint-discovery regression, not a failed gateway: update through a Rook release containing the corrected Ceph dashboard behavior, then have the reporter verify the Object Gateway page before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Use the Ceph upgrade procedure or Rook 1.13.1, which packages Ceph v18.2.1 with the endpoint fix. After upgrading, open the Object Gateway page and confirm that it reaches RGW through the Kubernetes-accessible endpoint. Do not force a downgrade to v17.2.5; the reporter's monitors crashed on that path.
solution.inference_hint: The raw evidence establishes that a working RGW is discovered as a Kubernetes node hostname on port 8080 and that the manager's admin request is refused. Mapping this to the Ceph dashboard endpoint-discovery behavior introduced in v17.2.6, and to the later Ceph correction packaged by Rook, is the maintainers' diagnosis from c3, c16, c24, c35-c36, and c40-c43. The final accepted diagnosis is the hostname/endpoint issue; c35's separate rgw-admin concern was explicitly withdrawn in c36.

edges.comment: Technical resolution follows c24 and c35-c36, with c40-c43 reporting the corrected Ceph behavior and its packaging in Rook. The original reporter never confirmed an upgrade or successful retest, so the terminal state records fix availability without claiming reporter-verified resolution.

solution.intent: Recognize the known Ceph dashboard RGW endpoint-discovery regression, update through a Rook release containing the corrected Ceph behavior, and require a dashboard retest before declaring success.
solution.concrete_example: This can occur when the Ceph dashboard discovers RGW through an endpoint that is not reachable from the manager in Kubernetes. Upgrade to a Rook/Ceph build containing the endpoint correction, then retest the Object Gateway page and report the result.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the thread's accepted fix immediately from the recognizable upgrade symptom. It skips the manager-log, node-identity, Ceph-version, and failed-rollback evidence gathered in the actual diagnostic chain.

edges.comment: Required shortcut from the start because the reporter's first attempted remedy was the falsified rollback. It preserves a match for an agent that proposes the accepted update path immediately, while still requiring user verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as a Ceph dashboard RGW endpoint-discovery regression: the manager tries an unreachable Kubernetes node hostname and RGW port instead of an endpoint reachable through the Kubernetes gateway service.
Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence that RGW still serves requests while the manager's RGW admin request to a node hostname on port 8080 is refused.
Must recommend updating through a Rook or Ceph build containing the corrected dashboard endpoint handling rather than treating the gateway itself as unconfigured.
Must not recommend downgrading to the previous Ceph stack as the resolution; that attempt caused the reporter's monitors to abort while decoding authentication state.
Must ask the reporter to retest the Object Gateway dashboard on a build containing the fix and must not declare the original reporter's cluster resolved until that verification is reported.

persona_hint.experience_level: Kubernetes and Helm cluster operator with practical Rook/Ceph experience; comfortable upgrading charts, reading pod logs, and identifying node names, but relies on maintainers for component-specific diagnostics and safe Ceph upgrade guidance.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, direct, and cooperative; supplies exact log excerpts when told which component to inspect, confirms matching failures, and asks practical questions about safe upgrade or rollback paths.
